title: Spatial scale space from hemigroup axioms: rotation-invariant self-decomposable kernels in dimension d
description:
Scale-space axioms usually require the cascade to be a semigroup, which with rotation and scale invariance leads to Gaussian and stable kernels. The axioms studied here require only that the stages compose, a hemigroup indexed by two scales, and that rescaling the signal relabels the scales. This paper derives the rotation-invariant families they allow in ℝ^d. The kernels that take the signal to each scale are the dilations of one rotation-invariant law that is self-decomposable: the convolution of each contracted copy of itself with another law. Every such law but the point mass occurs. Suitably labelled, the kernel at scale t has Fourier transform e^{-F(t|ξ|)}, for one function F. Its density is bounded near the centre exactly when c > d, where c ≤ ∞ is the power at which the transform falls off. Otherwise a point source is recorded as a spike, whose growth and constant are given. For finite c a stage between positive scales passes a fixed fraction of the record unchanged. Since c depends on F alone, a kernel bounded on the line can have a spike in the plane: the Matérn kernels of the Bessel scale space, with transform (1 + |ξ|^2/2)^{-γ}, do for 1/2 < γ ≤ 1. Each higher dimension allows strictly fewer F. An allowed F(r) ∼ c log r determines a radial characteristic function, the Fourier transform of a law, and is allowed in ℝ^{d+1} exactly when that function is a characteristic function there. The statements are machine-checked in Lean 4, assuming seven theorems of the literature, except those that § 1.1 lists as proved in print.

This deposit is the article's verification export: the PDF, its LaTeX source, the Lean 4 modules its statements rest on, the trust boundary with the ledger of cited facts, the blueprint chapters, the process account and the external reviews.
